name: AcousticGuard: sub-$15 machine-fault listener on a microcontroller
problem: Small factories, pump houses and agri-processing units cannot afford condition monitoring, so motors and bearings fail without warning.
verify: Find MSME downtime/maintenance-cost surveys; interview 3 workshop owners; check what vendors charge per sensor node.
existing: Commercial vibration nodes (hundreds of USD, cloud-tied); academic CWRU/MIMII dataset papers that rarely test on cheap MEMS mics.
idea: Unsupervised on-device anomaly model on a MEMS microphone/accelerometer; learns each machine's own 'normal' in-situ, no labelled faults needed.
novelty: Hypothesis: per-machine self-calibrating autoencoder on <512KB RAM that is evaluated across mic placement shift, which most papers skip. Must verify vs. TinyML anomaly-detection literature.
stack: ESP32-S3 or RP2040, I2S MEMS mic, ADXL345, TFLite Micro / Edge Impulse, Python for training, MQTT optional
stages: Collect baseline audio from a fan/pump rig -> train autoencoder -> quantize to int8 -> run on MCU -> inject faults (loosen mount, add imbalance) -> measure detection latency/false alarms
hw: ESP32-S3, MEMS mic, accelerometer, a fan or small pump
risks: Domain shift between rigs; noisy environments; false alarms erode trust.
metrics: AUROC on injected faults, false alarms/day, RAM/flash, mW, detection delay

name: Q-Ready: cryptographic bill of materials scanner for post-quantum migration
problem: Organisations do not know where RSA/ECC is used in code, certificates and protocols, so they cannot plan migration to NIST PQC standards.
verify: Read NIST IR 8547 timeline and CISA/NSA PQC guidance; survey public statements on 'crypto inventory' as the first migration blocker.
existing: IBM CBOM/Sonar crypto plugins, commercial discovery tools; most focus on source scanning, fewer correlate live TLS endpoints + binaries + config.
idea: One tool that scans repos, container images and live TLS endpoints, emits a CycloneDX CBOM, and ranks assets by 'harvest-now-decrypt-later' exposure (data lifetime x algorithm).
novelty: Hypothesis: exposure-ranking by data shelf-life across the three scan surfaces. Check CycloneDX CBOM tooling and commercial scanners first.
stack: Python, tree-sitter, sslyze/OpenSSL, CycloneDX schema, SQLite, small web UI
stages: Static crypto-API detectors -> TLS handshake prober -> CBOM export -> exposure scoring -> evaluate on 20 open-source repos
risks: False positives from wrapper libraries; legal limits on scanning third-party hosts (scan only your own/permitted).
metrics: Precision/recall vs hand-labelled repos, scan time, CBOM schema validity

name: MicroTexture: phone-camera authentication of paper/packaging without special ink
problem: Counterfeit medicines and branded goods are costly and dangerous; QR codes and holograms are trivially copied.
verify: Find OECD/EUIPO counterfeit trade estimates and WHO falsified-medicine reports; compare cost per unit of existing tags.
existing: Holograms, serialised QR, NFC tags, PUF research (needs lab imaging), startups using AI on printed dot patterns.
idea: Treat the natural random fibre/ink texture of each package as a fingerprint; enrol with a macro photo, verify with a phone, bind to a signed record.
novelty: Hypothesis: robust matching across phone models and lighting using learned descriptors + signature binding. Large prior art on 'paper fingerprinting' - must differentiate on phone robustness evidence.
stack: Python/OpenCV, PyTorch (metric learning), Ed25519 signatures, FastAPI, Flutter/PWA
stages: Build image set (100 samples x 5 phones x 3 lights) -> baseline SIFT/ORB -> learned descriptor -> FAR/FRR curve -> signed enrolment service
risks: Print variance, wear, adversarial reprints; needs rigorous FAR/FRR.
metrics: EER, FAR at fixed FRR, robustness across devices

name: FloodNet: store-and-forward LoRa mesh with triage messages for disaster zones
problem: Cell networks fail in floods/cyclones exactly when people need to report needs and rescuers need a picture.
verify: Read NDMA/post-disaster telecom outage reports; check Meshtastic limits for structured messages.
existing: Meshtastic (chat-oriented), satellite messengers, ham radio.
idea: Structured, priority-aware messages (medical, water, rescue) with deduplication and geo-aggregation on a LoRa mesh, plus a responder map at any connected node.
novelty: Hypothesis: priority + CRDT-style aggregation so a congested low-bandwidth mesh stays useful. Check Meshtastic plugins and DisasterRadio-style projects.
stack: ESP32 + SX1262, Meshtastic firmware or RadioLib, Python simulator, Leaflet map
stages: Simulate congestion in Python -> prototype 3-5 nodes -> implement priority/dedup -> range and delivery tests outdoors -> responder UI
risks: RF regulations (use ISM 865-867 MHz in India), range variance.
metrics: Delivery ratio vs node count, latency, airtime utilisation

name: CropDoctor Offline: calibrated plant-disease triage that says 'I don't know'
problem: Farmers with poor connectivity misdiagnose crop disease; apps trained on clean lab images (PlantVillage) fail in field conditions and are overconfident.
verify: Find yield-loss-from-pests estimates (FAO/ICAR); read papers documenting PlantVillage-to-field performance drops.
existing: Plantix, Kisan apps, many PlantVillage CNN demos.
idea: On-phone model with out-of-distribution rejection and conformal prediction sets; outputs 'uncertain - take a second photo/see extension officer' instead of a wrong label.
novelty: Hypothesis: honest uncertainty + field-image benchmark you collect. Value is the evaluation (lab vs field), not another CNN.
stack: PyTorch, MobileNet/EfficientNet-Lite, TFLite, conformal prediction (MAPIE), PWA/Android
stages: Reproduce baseline -> collect 300+ field photos -> measure drop -> add OOD + conformal -> int8 on-phone -> field test with a farmer/extension worker
risks: Field data collection effort; label noise; liability (advisory only).
metrics: Accuracy on field set, coverage vs set size, OOD AUROC, latency on mid-range phone
prior_art: plant disease detection field images domain shift

name: TaintGuard: information-flow control for LLM agents against prompt injection
problem: Agents that read web pages/emails and call tools can be hijacked by instructions hidden in untrusted data.
verify: Review OWASP LLM Top 10, AgentDojo and recent incident reports; measure baseline attack success rate yourself.
existing: Heuristic filters, guard models, CaMeL-style capability/dual-LLM designs, AgentDojo benchmark.
idea: Tag every value with provenance (trusted/untrusted); a deterministic policy engine blocks tool calls whose arguments derive from untrusted data unless user-approved.
novelty: Hypothesis: lightweight taint layer pluggable into MCP servers with measurable utility/security trade-off. Strong prior art (CaMeL, FIDES) - contribution would be implementation + benchmark.
stack: Python, MCP SDK, AgentDojo, pydantic policies
stages: Run AgentDojo baseline -> implement taint propagation -> policy DSL -> measure attack success vs task success -> publish results
risks: Utility loss from over-blocking; taint through LLM summarisation is hard to define.
metrics: Attack success rate, benign task completion, user-approval prompts per task

name: PkgDiff: behavioural diffing of npm/PyPI releases to catch supply-chain malware
problem: Malicious package updates (hijacked maintainers, install-script payloads) reach developers before registries remove them.
verify: Pull public incident lists (e.g. Socket, Phylum, OpenSSF malicious-packages) and compute time-to-removal.
existing: Socket, Phylum, OSV malicious-packages, Scorecard, GuardDog.
idea: Diff version N vs N-1 for new capabilities (network, exec, env access, obfuscation, new install hooks) and score the change, sandbox-run the delta.
novelty: Hypothesis: capability-delta scoring plus sandbox trace of only the changed code. Check GuardDog/Socket for the same approach.
stack: Python, tree-sitter/AST, Docker/gVisor sandbox, OSV malicious-packages dataset
stages: Build labelled set from OpenSSF dataset -> static capability extractor -> delta scoring -> sandbox traces -> measure precision at fixed alert budget
risks: Ethics: detonate only in isolated sandbox, never publish live malware; evasion by attackers.
metrics: Precision@k, recall on known-malicious set, scan time per package

name: EvidenceTrail: provenance-linked LLM assistant for digital forensic timelines
problem: Investigators drown in log/artifact volume, and LLM summaries are unusable as evidence because claims cannot be traced to raw artifacts.
verify: Read DFIR practitioner posts and SANS surveys on workload; check admissibility guidance on AI-derived output.
existing: Plaso/log2timeline, Timesketch, Velociraptor; LLM add-ons without citations.
idea: Every sentence the assistant produces must cite artifact IDs; an automatic verifier rejects uncited or contradicted claims.
novelty: Hypothesis: enforced citation + verifier loop on top of Timesketch data. Check Timesketch LLM features.
stack: Python, Plaso, Timesketch/OpenSearch, LLM API, claim-verifier module
stages: Ingest public DFIR challenge images -> timeline -> retrieval -> cited answers -> verifier -> score against ground-truth findings
risks: Hallucinated citations; sensitive data handling; verifier false rejects.
metrics: Claim-support rate, findings recall vs challenge answer key, time saved

name: HydroPing: low-cost pressure-transient sensors to localise pipe leaks
problem: Large fractions of treated water are lost to leaks (non-revenue water); finding where is slow and manual.
verify: Find CPHEEO/World Bank NRW figures for Indian cities; confirm cost of acoustic correlators.
existing: Acoustic correlators, satellite leak detection, expensive SCADA.
idea: Time-synchronised cheap pressure sensors capture transient waves; arrival-time differences localise the leak or burst.
novelty: Hypothesis: GPS/PPS-synced MCU nodes at <INR 3k each reach usable localisation error. Needs bench validation with a pipe loop.
stack: RP2040/ESP32, 0-10 bar pressure transducer, GPS PPS or NTP-disciplined clock, Python localisation
stages: Simulate wave propagation -> bench test on a pipe loop with a controllable valve leak -> measure localisation error -> field trial in a building
risks: Clock sync accuracy, wave speed uncertainty, safety around water pressure.
metrics: Localisation error (m), detection threshold (L/min), false triggers
prior_art: pressure transient leak localisation low cost
IoT water leak detection time difference of arrival

name: DigesterWatch: sensing and early-warning for community biogas digesters
problem: Small digesters fail silently (acidification, temperature drop), losing gas output and farmer trust.
verify: Search biogas plant failure/abandonment rates in India (e.g. NBMMP reviews); interview a plant operator.
existing: Industrial SCADA, manual pH/temperature checks.
idea: Low-cost pH/temperature/gas-pressure/CH4 sensing with a simple rule+trend model that warns days before failure.
novelty: Hypothesis: practical early-warning features from cheap sensors; mostly an applied engineering project, state this honestly.
stack: ESP32, DS18B20, pH probe, MQ-4/NDIR CH4, Grafana/Telegram alerts
stages: Sensor characterisation -> logger -> 4-week digester run (even a lab-scale one) -> alert rules -> evaluate lead time
risks: Sensor drift in corrosive gas; slow biological timescales.
metrics: Alert lead time, false alerts, sensor drift/week

name: ReproBench: automatic reproducibility harness for ML papers
problem: Many papers cannot be re-run: missing seeds, pinned versions or data, so claimed gains cannot be checked.
verify: Cite ML Reproducibility Challenge reports; sample 20 recent repos and record how many run unmodified.
existing: Papers with Code, ReproZip, Docker templates, MLRC.
idea: Tool that builds an environment from a repo, runs the declared command, compares reported vs reproduced metrics, and publishes a reproducibility card.
novelty: Hypothesis: automated environment inference + metric diff. Evidence needed on success rate.
stack: Python, Docker, uv/pip-compile, GitHub API, small LLM for README parsing (optional)
stages: Sample 30 repos -> manual baseline run rate -> automate env build -> automate metric compare -> publish report
risks: GPU/data availability; running untrusted repos needs sandboxing.
metrics: % repos reproduced automatically, time per repo

name: GazeCursor: webcam eye-control for people with motor impairment
problem: Eye trackers cost USD 150-2000; many people with ALS/spinal injury cannot afford them.
verify: Find assistive-tech cost surveys; talk to an occupational therapist or disability NGO.
existing: Tobii, Camera Mouse, WebGazer.js, Google Project Gameface.
idea: Per-user calibrated gaze+head-pose model with dwell/blink click and error-correcting on-screen targets, running fully in the browser.
novelty: Hypothesis: accuracy gain from continual self-calibration using click feedback. Prior art strong (Gameface, WebGazer) - focus on measured accuracy.
stack: MediaPipe FaceMesh, TF.js/ONNX Web, WebGL, Kalman smoothing
stages: Baseline WebGazer accuracy -> collect calibration data from 5 volunteers -> online recalibration -> accessibility usability test
risks: Lighting, glasses, fatigue; must test with real target users.
metrics: Angular error (deg), target hit rate, words/min on virtual keyboard
prior_art: webcam eye tracking calibration deep learning

name: BridgeEar: vibration-based health monitoring for old buildings and small bridges
problem: Ageing bridges and buildings are inspected visually and rarely; collapses give little warning.
verify: Gather bridge-collapse statistics and inspection-frequency policy; read SHM review papers.
existing: Fibre/strain gauge systems costing lakhs, periodic visual inspection.
idea: Cheap accelerometer nodes estimate natural frequencies (operational modal analysis) and flag frequency drift beyond environmental/temperature effects.
novelty: Hypothesis: temperature-compensated frequency tracking with MEMS accelerometers. Validate on a lab beam first.
stack: ESP32 + ADXL355/MPU, Python (scipy, FDD/SSI), temperature compensation regression
stages: Cantilever beam rig -> add mass/crack to shift frequency -> compensate temperature -> detect shift -> try on a footbridge
risks: MEMS noise floor, environmental confounders, never claim safety certification.
metrics: Frequency resolution (Hz), detection of known stiffness change, false alarm rate
prior_art: operational modal analysis MEMS low cost

name: SideChannel Lab: power-analysis attacks on your own microcontroller
problem: Embedded crypto implementations leak keys through power; most developers never test for it.
verify: Review published SCA attacks on commodity MCUs; confirm cost of commercial testing.
existing: ChipWhisperer, commercial labs.
idea: Build a cheap capture rig and reproduce CPA on AES in your own board, then evaluate masking countermeasures with a TVLA leakage test.
novelty: Level-3/5 research-replication: value is the measured comparison, not a new attack. Attack only hardware you own.
stack: ChipWhisperer-Lite/Nano or oscilloscope + shunt, Python (numpy), STM32/AVR targets
stages: Capture traces -> CPA recover key from unprotected AES -> add masking -> TVLA t-test -> write results
risks: Equipment cost; time sink; keep to own devices.
metrics: Traces needed for key recovery, TVLA t-values pre/post masking

name: FirmLens: SBOM and CVE matching from router/IoT firmware images
problem: Consumers and small vendors cannot tell which outdated components (BusyBox, OpenSSL) sit inside their devices.
verify: Use CISA KEV and vendor advisories to show component-based vulnerabilities in IoT.
existing: EMBA, FACT, Binwalk, commercial SCA.
idea: Extract firmware, fingerprint library versions from binaries, map to CVEs with exploitability context and produce a readable report for non-experts.
novelty: Hypothesis: better version fingerprinting and plain-language prioritisation. Existing open tools (EMBA/FACT) are strong - compare accuracy directly.
stack: Python, binwalk/unblob, YARA, NVD/OSV API, CycloneDX
stages: Collect 20 open firmware images -> extractor -> version fingerprints -> CVE mapping -> compare vs EMBA ground truth
risks: Legal use of firmware images; NVD data noise.
metrics: Component identification precision/recall vs known SBOM

name: CoughCheck: rigorous domain-shift evaluation of audio respiratory screening
problem: Cough-based screening papers report high accuracy that collapses on new devices/hospitals.
verify: Read systematic reviews on cough-AI bias; list datasets (Coswara, COUGHVID) and their collection protocols.
existing: Papers and startups claiming TB/COVID cough detection.
idea: A negative-result-friendly study: train on one dataset, test across devices/sites, and publish honest performance plus a mitigation (domain adaptation).
novelty: Hypothesis: a careful cross-dataset benchmark is itself useful. No clinical claims.
stack: Python, torchaudio, public datasets, scikit-learn
stages: Reproduce paper -> cross-dataset test -> domain adaptation -> report with confidence intervals
risks: Data licences; must not be framed as diagnostic.
metrics: AUROC in-domain vs cross-domain, calibration error
prior_art: cough audio covid detection bias review

name: VaaniDispatch: low-bandwidth voice triage for emergency calls in Indian languages
problem: Call-takers handle mixed-language, noisy calls; transcription and structured intake are slow.
verify: Study 112/ERSS public documents and response-time reports; talk to a dispatcher if possible.
existing: Commercial CAD systems, Whisper/Indic ASR models, AI4Bharat IndicConformer.
idea: Streaming Indic ASR + slot extraction (location, condition) with human-in-the-loop confirmation, evaluated on noisy code-mixed audio.
novelty: Hypothesis: evaluation on noisy code-mixed emergency-style speech with entity-level accuracy. Use only synthetic/consented data.
stack: AI4Bharat models, faster-whisper, spaCy/LLM slot filling, WebSocket UI
stages: Create scripted test calls in 3 languages -> ASR WER baseline -> entity extraction -> UI -> measure intake time
risks: Privacy; safety-critical so assistive only; dataset creation effort.
metrics: WER, entity F1 (address, injury), intake time saved

name: RoadSense: dashcam edge mapping of potholes and missing signs
problem: Road defects are reported manually; municipalities lack current condition maps.
verify: Road-accident statistics linked to road condition (MoRTH); compare to complaint-system latency.
existing: RDD2022 dataset models, Mapillary, commercial road-survey vans.
idea: On-device detector + GPS tagging with temporal clustering of repeat detections to cut false positives, output GeoJSON for authorities.
novelty: Hypothesis: multi-pass clustering and Indian-road evaluation. Prior art is large; evaluation on local data is the contribution.
stack: YOLO-nano/RT-DETR, Jetson/RPi or phone, OpenStreetMap, DBSCAN
stages: Train on RDD2022 -> drive-collect local clips -> measure drop -> clustering -> map output
risks: Mounting/safety; motion blur; privacy blur for faces/plates.
metrics: mAP local vs RDD, precision after clustering, FPS on device

name: ColdProof: tamper-evident temperature logger with signed readings
problem: Spoiled vaccines/food are hard to dispute because paper or CSV logs can be edited.
verify: WHO/Gavi cold-chain failure estimates; food-loss figures (FAO).
existing: Commercial loggers with cloud portals, blockchain pilots.
idea: MCU hashes-chain and signs every reading with a hardware-held key (ATECC608/secure element); verifier detects gaps, edits and replays offline.
novelty: Hypothesis: offline-verifiable signed chain without blockchain. Simpler than blockchain approaches.
stack: ESP32/nRF, ATECC608A, DS18B20/SHT4x, Ed25519/ECDSA, Python verifier
stages: Logger firmware -> hash chain -> signing -> tamper test (edit/replay/delete) -> verifier CLI -> power-fail tests
risks: Key provisioning/rotation; physical sensor spoofing remains.
metrics: Tamper detection rate, power-loss data integrity, battery life
prior_art: tamper evident logging hash chain embedded

name: SecureGen: measuring vulnerabilities in LLM-written code with executable exploit tests
problem: LLM code assistants emit insecure patterns, but many benchmarks use static scanners with high false positives.
verify: Read CyberSecEval, SecurityEval and recent studies; measure your own baseline.
existing: CyberSecEval, SecurityEval, CodeLMSec, static analyzers.
idea: Benchmark tasks that include runnable exploit tests (not just pattern matching) for ~40 CWEs, compare models with and without security prompts.
novelty: Hypothesis: executable exploit oracles reduce false positives. Prior art exists - compare methodology.
stack: Python, Docker, pytest, Semgrep/CodeQL for comparison, model APIs
stages: Pick 20 CWEs -> write tasks + exploit tests -> run models -> compare to Semgrep verdicts -> report agreement
risks: Task leakage into training data; exploit tests need sandboxing.
metrics: Vulnerable-rate per model, agreement with static tools
prior_art: LLM generated code security empirical study

name: VoiceShield: on-device detection of AI-cloned voices in scam calls
problem: Voice-clone scams impersonate relatives/officials; victims have seconds to decide.
verify: Use NCRB/I4C cyber-fraud statistics and press cases; check ASVspoof generalisation results.
existing: ASVspoof countermeasure papers, commercial call-screening services.
idea: Lightweight spoof detector plus out-of-distribution scoring, evaluated honestly on unseen TTS systems and compressed telephony audio.
novelty: Hypothesis: telephony codec (8 kHz, AMR) robustness. Detection of unseen generators is an open problem - expect limited results and report them.
stack: PyTorch, torchaudio, AASIST/RawNet baselines, ONNX Runtime Mobile
stages: Reproduce AASIST -> add codec augmentation -> test on unseen generators -> quantize -> on-phone demo
risks: Arms race; high false positives; privacy of call audio (on-device only).
metrics: EER on unseen generators, EER after codec, latency

name: SunTwin: digital twin and fault detector for a small solar microgrid
problem: Rural/campus solar plants lose output from soiling, shading and failing strings that go unnoticed.
verify: Find PV underperformance statistics (NREL/NISE reports); check monitoring costs.
existing: Inverter portals, pvlib models, commercial O&M analytics.
idea: pvlib-based expected-output twin; residual analysis flags soiling vs shading vs string faults using irradiance and string-level currents.
novelty: Hypothesis: fault classification from residual signatures using only commodity sensors. Validate on real system data or public PV datasets.
stack: pvlib, Python, ESP32 + INA219/INA226 string sensors, InfluxDB/Grafana
stages: Model baseline on public data -> residual detector -> hardware string monitor -> inject shading faults -> classify
hw: Small PV panel + MPPT + current sensors
risks: Weather model error; limited fault diversity.
metrics: Fault classification accuracy, energy-loss estimate error

name: OrbitWatch: anomaly detection on open amateur satellite telemetry
problem: Small satellites lose missions to undetected subsystem degradation; open telemetry is underused.
verify: Review CubeSat failure-rate studies (e.g. Langer & Bouwmeester, Swartwout).
existing: NASA SMAP/MSL anomaly benchmarks, ESA OPS-SAT data.
idea: Decode public SatNOGS telemetry, build per-satellite baselines, and detect drift/battery degradation; compare against NASA SMAP-style methods.
novelty: Hypothesis: open, real-world, multi-satellite benchmark rather than the controversial SMAP labels. Mostly an evaluation contribution.
stack: Python, SatNOGS DB API, gr-satellites decoders, scikit-learn/PyOD
stages: Pull telemetry for 5 satellites -> decode -> feature engineering -> detectors -> compare w/ known anomaly events
risks: Sparse sampling, no ground truth labels, decoder variety.
metrics: Event detection rate vs known outages, false alarms per orbit-day

name: HonestPINN: fair benchmark of physics-informed networks against classical solvers
problem: Papers claim PINNs/neural operators beat classical solvers but compare against weak baselines.
verify: Read 'Challenges in training PINNs' and recent baseline-critique papers (e.g. Grossmann et al.).
existing: PDEBench, NVIDIA Modulus, DeepXDE.
idea: Equal-compute, equal-accuracy comparison on heat/Burgers/Navier-Stokes problems against tuned FEM/FVM, reporting cost to target error.
novelty: Hypothesis: rigorous cost-to-accuracy curves for a few problems. Contribution is evidence, not a new model.
stack: JAX/PyTorch, DeepXDE/Modulus, FEniCSx, matplotlib
stages: Implement 3 PDEs -> tuned classical baseline -> PINN/FNO -> compute-matched plots -> write-up
risks: Tuning bias on both sides.
metrics: Error vs wall-clock, training+inference cost, parameter sensitivity
prior_art: neural operator vs classical solver comparison

name: PatchLag: knowledge graph of CVE -> exploit -> patch -> advisory delays
problem: Defenders prioritise poorly; time between disclosure, exploit availability and patch varies widely per vendor and is rarely visible.
verify: Use CISA KEV, EPSS and Exploit-DB; compute your own lag distributions.
existing: EPSS, VulnCheck KEV, Vulners.
idea: Open graph linking CVEs, exploits, patches, vendor advisories and KEV listings with per-vendor lag statistics and a simple prioritiser.
novelty: Hypothesis: transparent vendor-lag stats; compare to EPSS predictive value on held-out months.
stack: Python, PostgreSQL/Neo4j, NVD/OSV/KEV/Exploit-DB feeds, Streamlit
stages: Ingest feeds -> entity resolution -> lag metrics -> prioritiser -> backtest vs EPSS
risks: Data inconsistencies; API rate limits.
metrics: Backtest AUC for 'exploited within 30 days', graph coverage

name: PrivFed: federated learning with measured privacy-attack leakage
problem: Hospitals cannot share patient data; federated learning is promoted as safe but gradients can leak records.
verify: Read gradient inversion and membership-inference literature; check regulation context (DPDP Act).
existing: Flower, NVIDIA FLARE, OpenFL.
idea: Simulate multi-site federated training on chest X-ray/ECG data, attack it, and plot utility vs privacy budget under DP-SGD and secure aggregation.
novelty: Hypothesis: empirical privacy/utility frontier on realistic non-IID splits. Evaluation-driven.
stack: Flower, Opacus, PyTorch, public datasets (CheXpert/PhysioNet access rules)
stages: Centralised baseline -> federated -> membership/gradient attacks -> DP -> frontier plot
risks: Dataset access terms; compute.
metrics: Attack AUC, accuracy vs epsilon

name: RoverInspect: low-cost ROS 2 inspection rover with SLAM accuracy benchmark
problem: Inspecting ducts, basements and farm sheds is hazardous; commercial inspection robots are expensive.
verify: Price research for commercial inspection robots; interview a maintenance team about inspection tasks.
existing: Boston Dynamics Spot, Clearpath, hobby ROS rovers.
idea: A documented sub-INR 40k rover whose SLAM/odometry error is measured against a ground-truth tape-measure/AprilTag setup, with fault-tolerant autonomy.
novelty: Hypothesis: reproducible low-cost benchmark protocol. Not novel hardware - rigour is the contribution.
stack: ROS 2, Nav2, slam_toolbox, RPLidar/LD19, ESP32 motor controller, IMU
stages: Teleop -> odometry + IMU fusion -> SLAM -> Nav2 -> accuracy trials with AprilTags -> fault tests
risks: Mechanical debugging time; ROS tuning.
metrics: ATE (m), loop-closure error, mission success rate

name: AttestMini: lightweight remote attestation for ESP32 fleets
problem: IoT fleets cannot prove that a device runs unmodified firmware, enabling silent compromise.
verify: Review IoT botnet incidents and the ETSI EN 303 645 / EU CRA requirements.
existing: TPM/DICE attestation, AWS IoT Device Defender, ESP32 secure boot+flash encryption.
idea: Challenge-response attestation of firmware hash with eFuse-bound keys, plus a verifier that gates network access.
novelty: Hypothesis: practical ESP32-class implementation with measured overhead; prior art in DICE/SEDA must be cited.
stack: ESP-IDF, secure boot v2, mbedTLS, Python verifier/FastAPI
stages: Enable secure boot -> measured boot hash -> signed challenge response -> attack demos (modified firmware) -> overhead measurement
hw: 2-3 ESP32 boards (eFuses are irreversible - use sacrificial boards)
risks: Bricking boards; limited protection against physical attackers.
metrics: Attack detection, attestation time, memory overhead

name: ElephantEye: acoustic + camera early warning for crop-raiding wildlife
problem: Elephant/boar crop-raiding causes crop loss and fatalities in India; fences and watchmen are costly and unreliable.
verify: Find MoEFCC human-elephant conflict fatality/crop-damage data; read pilot studies of camera/seismic alerts.
existing: Camera-trap AI, Zooniverse, thermal-camera fences, SMS alert pilots.
idea: Solar edge node that fuses infrared camera detections with infrasonic/acoustic cues and sends LoRa alerts to farmers with false-alarm rate reported.
novelty: Hypothesis: multi-sensor fusion at low power. Several pilots exist - differentiator is measured false-alarm/latency.
stack: Jetson Nano/RPi + PIR/thermal, YOLO-nano, LoRa, solar + LiFePO4
stages: Public camera-trap datasets -> detector -> power budget -> field node -> alert latency tests with livestock/people proxy
hw: RPi/Jetson, thermal or IR cam, LoRa, solar
risks: Field deployment access, permissions from forest dept, weatherproofing.
metrics: Detection range, false alarms/night, alert latency, battery autonomy
prior_art: elephant detection camera trap deep learning
human wildlife conflict early warning India

name: EdgeLLM-Joules: energy/latency/accuracy frontier of small LLMs on phones and Pi
problem: Claims about on-device LLMs rarely report energy per token or accuracy loss under quantisation on real hardware.
verify: Survey existing mobile LLM benchmark papers; list what they omit.
existing: llama.cpp benchmarks, MLC-LLM, MLPerf Tiny/Mobile.
idea: Measure tokens/s, J/token and task accuracy across quantisation levels on RPi5, a phone and a laptop with an inline power meter, publish reproducible scripts.
novelty: Hypothesis: complete energy-accuracy-latency Pareto data on cheap hardware. Evaluation-driven.
stack: llama.cpp, lm-eval-harness, USB power meter, Python
stages: Pick 4 models x 4 quants -> instrument power -> run tasks -> Pareto plots -> publish
risks: Thermal throttling variance.
metrics: J/token, tokens/s, accuracy delta
prior_art: quantization accuracy small language models edge

name: OriginTrace: find the original source behind syndicated news claims
problem: The same unverified claim is reprinted by dozens of outlets, creating false 'multiple confirmations'.
verify: Read studies on syndication/circular reporting; sample 50 viral stories and count independent origins.
existing: Fact-check databases, plagiarism detectors, Google Fact Check API.
idea: Near-duplicate clustering with embeddings and temporal ordering to estimate the earliest source and count truly independent sources.
novelty: Hypothesis: independent-source counting metric. Also a core module for the NEXUS agent itself.
stack: Python, sentence-transformers, MinHash/LSH, SQLite/pgvector
stages: Collect feeds -> dedup -> cluster -> origin estimation -> manual label 100 clusters -> evaluate
risks: Paywalls, rewrite-heavy copies.
metrics: Origin accuracy vs manual labels, cluster purity

name: BeatGuard: explainable edge arrhythmia screening with dataset-shift tests
problem: Atrial fibrillation is under-detected; ECG models often fail on different devices/populations.
verify: AF prevalence/stroke-risk statistics; PhysioNet Challenge 2017/2021 findings.
existing: Apple Watch/KardiaMobile, PhysioNet challenge models.
idea: Tiny 1D-CNN/classical feature model on MCU with signal-quality gating and cross-database evaluation, with human-readable rhythm features.
novelty: Hypothesis: signal-quality gating reduces false positives on low-cost AD8232 hardware. Not a medical device.
stack: AD8232/ADS1292, ESP32, TFLite Micro, wfdb
stages: Reproduce PhysioNet baseline -> cross-DB test -> MCU deployment -> collect own ECG (self, with care) -> compare
risks: Safety (battery-powered, isolated only), no clinical claims.
metrics: F1 AF vs normal across DBs, FP rate after gating, flash/RAM

name: RedactLocal: in-browser PII redaction for documents, nothing uploaded
problem: People upload ID documents to random online tools to redact them, leaking the very data they want to protect.
verify: Look for privacy incidents involving online document tools; measure how many redaction sites upload files (network tab).
existing: Cloud redactors, Acrobat, some local desktop tools.
idea: Entirely client-side OCR + regex/NER redaction (Aadhaar, PAN, phone, address) with irreversible rasterised output, verified by an offline test that no network requests occur.
novelty: Hypothesis: verifiable no-upload guarantee (CSP + test). Product-level not research-level, valid as a 48h hackathon build.
stack: Tesseract.js/ONNX OCR, pdf.js, WASM, Service Worker, strict CSP
stages: OCR in browser -> PII detectors with Verhoeff check for Aadhaar -> redaction canvas -> CSP + network test -> accuracy eval on synthetic IDs
risks: OCR errors miss PII; must flag residual risk to the user.
metrics: PII recall/precision on synthetic set, zero network requests, time per page

name: GreenWave: adaptive traffic signals evaluated in SUMO against fixed-time baselines
problem: Fixed-time signals waste time and fuel; heterogeneous Indian traffic breaks many Western-trained models.
verify: Congestion cost studies; check SCATS/SCOOT existing deployment evidence.
existing: SCATS, SCOOT, RL papers (PressLight, CoLight).
idea: Pressure-based controller (non-RL) vs RL, with mixed two-wheeler traffic calibrated to real counts, reporting honest wins/losses.
novelty: Hypothesis: simple max-pressure may match RL on heterogeneous traffic. Useful negative result is acceptable.
stack: SUMO, TraCI, PyTorch/SB3, OSM networks
stages: Network from OSM -> calibrate demand -> baselines -> max-pressure -> RL -> compare delay/emissions
risks: Simulation-to-reality gap.
metrics: Mean delay, throughput, CO2 estimate
prior_art: max pressure vs reinforcement learning traffic signals

name: GridAware: carbon-intensity-aware scheduler for batch compute
problem: AI/batch jobs run when grid electricity is most carbon-intensive although many are deferrable.
verify: Use Electricity Maps/WattTime data to quantify day-to-day variation in India vs EU; read carbon-aware computing papers.
existing: Google carbon-aware computing, Carbon Aware SDK, Kubernetes KEDA operators.
idea: Scheduler plugin that delays/shifts jobs by deadline and forecast intensity, reports avoided emissions with uncertainty.
novelty: Hypothesis: low-effort implementation for small labs/cron. Mostly applied engineering; Indian-grid evaluation may be sparse in literature.
stack: Python, Carbon Aware SDK/ElectricityMaps API, Slurm/cron/K8s, Prometheus
stages: Collect intensity data -> simulate on job traces -> implement scheduler -> measure savings vs deadline misses
risks: Small savings on low-variance grids.
metrics: gCO2 avoided, deadline miss rate

name: MemBench: do LLM agents actually remember? long-horizon memory evaluation
problem: Agent 'memory' products are marketed without comparable evidence on recall, staleness and contradiction handling.
verify: Read LongMemEval/LoCoMo and compare to vendor claims.
existing: LongMemEval, LoCoMo, mem0, Zep, MemGPT.
idea: Open harness testing retrieval-based, summary-based and graph memories on updates, contradictions and temporal queries over simulated months.
novelty: Hypothesis: a contradiction/temporal-update suite exposes failures averages hide. Check LongMemEval's coverage first.
stack: Python, pgvector/SQLite, LLM APIs, pytest
stages: Replicate LongMemEval subset -> add update/contradiction cases -> compare 3 memory designs -> report
risks: LLM-judge bias; cost.
metrics: Accuracy by query type, staleness error, tokens used

name: KitTrace: cluster phishing sites into kits and campaigns by visual and DOM fingerprint
problem: Takedowns are whack-a-mole: each phishing URL is reported separately even though many share one kit.
verify: Pull OpenPhish/PhishTank public feeds and measure how many URLs share near-identical DOM/screenshot hashes.
existing: URLScan, PhishTank, commercial brand-protection services, academic phishing classifiers.
idea: Fingerprint pages (DOM structure hash + perceptual image hash + form field order), cluster them, and surface campaigns plus shared infrastructure.
novelty: Hypothesis: cheap clustering that cuts analyst workload per campaign. Compare with URLScan similarity features first.
stack: Python, Playwright (isolated VM), imagehash, HDBSCAN, CT-log stream
stages: Collect 5k feed URLs -> render safely -> fingerprints -> cluster -> measure cluster purity against hand labels
risks: Visit phishing pages only inside an isolated VM/container; respect feed terms of use.
metrics: Cluster purity, URLs per campaign, time to first cluster after a new kit appears

name: LeakRadar: find and rank leaked secrets in your own repositories and git history
problem: Developers commit API keys; scanners flood teams with false positives so real leaks get ignored.
verify: Read GitGuardian's State of Secrets Sprawl; run gitleaks on 20 repos you own or that are open and count false positives.
existing: gitleaks, trufflehog, GitHub secret scanning.
idea: Combine entropy, context and format checks to rank real leaks, with offline validity checks only (never call third-party APIs with found keys).
novelty: Hypothesis: context-aware ranking lowers false positives versus plain regex. Evaluate against gitleaks on a labelled set.
stack: Python, git, regex + small classifier, pre-commit hook
stages: Build labelled set (SecretBench) -> baseline gitleaks -> context features -> pre-commit integration
risks: Treat findings as sensitive; never use discovered keys.
metrics: Precision/recall vs gitleaks, alerts per 1000 commits
prior_art: secret detection machine learning false positives

name: TrackerGuard: detect hidden BLE trackers (AirTag-style stalking) from a phone or ESP32
problem: Cheap trackers are used for stalking and theft; detection support differs across phones and tag brands.
verify: Read Apple/Google detection specs, the IETF DULT draft and published tracker-stalking studies.
existing: Apple Tracker Detect, Google unknown-tracker alerts, AirGuard.
idea: A scanner that flags BLE identifiers persisting across your locations despite address rotation, covering non-Apple tags too.
novelty: Hypothesis: open, tag-agnostic detection with measured false positives in crowds. AirGuard is strong prior art; compare against it.
stack: ESP32 or Android BLE scanner, Python analysis, GPS, SQLite
stages: Collect scan logs with your own tags -> persistence heuristic -> walking/bus route tests -> tune false positives
hw: ESP32 or phone, trackers you own
risks: Address rotation; privacy of logged third-party devices (store hashes only).
metrics: Detection time for a followed tag, false alarms per hour in crowds

name: CanaryFS: early ransomware detection with decoy files and entropy tripwires
problem: Ransomware encrypts thousands of files before anyone notices; detection often comes too late.
verify: Read ransomware dwell-time reports (Sophos, Mandiant) and how fast encryptors hit network shares.
existing: EDR products, Windows Controlled Folder Access, canary-token services.
idea: Decoy files plus per-process write-entropy monitoring; on trigger, suspend the process and snapshot.
novelty: Hypothesis: low-overhead user-space tripwire with measured files-lost-before-stop. Test only with a harmless simulator you write, never live malware.
stack: Python or Rust, watchdog, psutil, a benign encryptor simulator
stages: Write simulator -> baseline monitoring -> decoys + entropy rule -> measure files lost and false positives (zip, backups)
risks: False positives on compression/backups; slow-encryption bypass.
metrics: Files lost before stop, CPU overhead, false positives per day

name: TunnelWatch: lightweight DNS tunneling and exfiltration detector for small networks
problem: Malware hides command-and-control and data theft inside DNS, which small networks rarely inspect.
verify: Read MITRE ATT&CK T1071.004 and published DNS-tunnel datasets.
existing: Zeek/Suricata rules, commercial DNS security, academic ML detectors.
idea: Per-domain features (query entropy, label length, rate, TXT usage) on a Raspberry Pi DNS sinkhole with explainable alerts.
novelty: Hypothesis: a tiny explainable model beats static thresholds at low false positives on a real home network.
stack: Raspberry Pi, Pi-hole/dnsmasq logs, Python, scikit-learn; dnscat2/iodine inside a lab VM for positives
stages: Collect 2 weeks benign logs -> generate tunnel traffic in a lab -> features -> detector -> review false positives
risks: DoH hides queries from your resolver; CDN false positives.
metrics: True-positive rate at 1 false positive/day, detection delay

name: PotWatch: low-interaction honeypot that turns attack logs into weekly threat intelligence
problem: Defenders rarely see what attackers try against small Indian infrastructure; global feeds miss local patterns.
verify: Review Cowrie/T-Pot research and CERT-In advisories; run one honeypot for a week and examine volume.
existing: T-Pot, Cowrie, GreyNoise, Shadowserver.
idea: Run sandboxed honeypots on a cloud free-tier VM, cluster attacker behaviour, and publish aggregated weekly stats (no victim data).
novelty: Hypothesis: region-specific insights and campaign clustering. Honeypots are common; novelty is in the analysis.
stack: Cowrie, Docker, SQLite/Elasticsearch, Python, GeoIP, MITRE ATT&CK mapping
stages: Deploy 1 honeypot -> collect 2 weeks -> session clustering -> weekly report -> add a second service
risks: Isolate strictly; never run on your home LAN; follow provider terms.
metrics: Unique attackers, campaigns identified, malware families captured

name: AirWatch: ESP32 sensor that detects evil-twin access points and deauth floods on your own network
problem: Fake Wi-Fi hotspots and deauthentication attacks steal credentials in cafes, hostels and offices.
verify: Read WIDS literature and 802.11w (PMF) adoption figures; test with your own access point.
existing: Enterprise WIDS (expensive), Kismet, WiFi-pineapple detection scripts.
idea: A passive monitor that learns your network's legitimate BSSID/channel/beacon fingerprint and alerts on clones and deauth bursts.
novelty: Hypothesis: beacon-timing and vendor-IE fingerprinting distinguishes clones cheaply. Test only against equipment you own.
stack: ESP32 promiscuous mode, Python collector, Telegram alerts, a spare router for the test
stages: Capture beacons -> baseline fingerprint -> simulate a clone with the spare AP -> lab deauth tests on your own AP -> thresholds
risks: Transmit attacks only on your own equipment; stay monitor-only otherwise.
metrics: Detection latency, false alarms per day

name: QRSafe: unwrap QR codes safely and score them before you open the link (UPI and payment scams)
problem: Scam QR codes (fake parking tickets, UPI collect requests, stickers pasted over real codes) lead to credential theft and payment fraud.
verify: Use I4C/RBI fraud statistics and recent quishing campaign reports; check what the phone camera shows before opening.
existing: Built-in camera link previews, antivirus QR scanners.
idea: On-device decoder that expands redirect chains in a sandboxed fetcher without cookies, parses UPI intents (payee, amount, pay vs collect) and warns on lookalike domains.
novelty: Hypothesis: UPI-intent-aware plain-language explanation is the differentiator. Product-level, well suited to a 48h build.
stack: PWA or Flutter, ML Kit/zxing, UPI URI parser, offline domain heuristics
stages: Decoder -> UPI parser -> redirect unwrapper -> heuristics -> test on 100 benign and malicious sample QRs -> UX with plain warnings
risks: Heuristic false positives; never fetch unknown URLs outside a sandbox.
metrics: Detection rate on the sample set, false warnings, time to verdict

name: MuleNet: graph analytics to flag money-mule account networks in payment data
problem: Fraud proceeds are moved through chains of mule accounts; per-transaction rules miss the network structure.
verify: Read RBI/I4C fraud statistics and published mule-detection literature; confirm what open synthetic datasets exist (e.g. PaySim, AMLSim).
existing: Bank rule engines, commercial graph fraud tools, academic GNN papers on synthetic data.
idea: Build a transaction graph on synthetic data, detect fan-in/fan-out and rapid-pass-through patterns, and compare simple graph features against a GNN with honest baselines.
novelty: Hypothesis: simple structural features nearly match GNNs at lower cost and are easier to explain. Use only synthetic or consented data.
stack: Python, NetworkX/igraph, PyTorch Geometric, scikit-learn, PaySim/AMLSim synthetic data
stages: Generate synthetic data -> rule baseline -> graph features -> GNN comparison -> explainability report -> false-positive analysis
risks: Synthetic data may not reflect reality; privacy and legal limits on real payment data.
metrics: Precision at fixed review budget, recall of ring members, explanation quality
prior_art: mule account detection graph neural network

name: SpoofScope: detect spoofing and layering patterns in public limit-order-book data
problem: Manipulative order patterns distort prices, and surveillance teams need transparent detectors rather than black boxes.
verify: Read regulator enforcement cases and market-surveillance papers; find open order-book datasets (sample LOBSTER data or public crypto-exchange feeds).
existing: Exchange surveillance systems (proprietary), academic anomaly papers.
idea: A research tool that labels order-cancel patterns via interpretable rules and compares them with an unsupervised detector on public data. It is a surveillance analytics tool, not a trading system.
novelty: Hypothesis: rule-plus-statistics hybrids are competitive and auditable. No claim about trading profit.
stack: Python, pandas/Polars, scikit-learn, public LOB or crypto exchange data
stages: Collect data -> reconstruct order book -> define patterns -> inject synthetic spoofing -> detect -> evaluate false positives
risks: No ground truth for real manipulation; labelled data is rare; never present results as investment advice.
metrics: Detection of injected patterns, false positives per trading day
prior_art: spoofing detection limit order book machine learning

name: PriceLens: nowcast food-price inflation from open price data
problem: Official price indices arrive with delay; early signals of food-price shocks matter for households and planners.
verify: Compare official CPI release lag with open daily price sources (e.g. government mandi/price portals); read the nowcasting literature.
existing: Central-bank nowcasts, scraped-price indices (Billion Prices Project style).
idea: Build a transparent nowcast from open daily commodity prices and test it against later official releases with proper out-of-sample evaluation.
novelty: Hypothesis: a small interpretable model competes with heavier ones for food items. An analytical tool, not a forecast service.
stack: Python, pandas, statsmodels, open government price data, backtesting harness
stages: Collect data -> clean -> baseline (last value, seasonal) -> model -> walk-forward backtest -> report errors
risks: Data gaps, terms of use for scraping, regime changes; no policy claims.
metrics: Error vs baseline (MAE/MASE), lead time over official release
prior_art: food price forecasting India mandi data

name: SupplierWatch: early warning of supplier disruption from public news and shipping signals
problem: Small manufacturers learn about supplier problems after delivery fails.
verify: Read supply-chain risk surveys; list free public signals (news, port data, weather).
existing: Resilinc, Everstream and other paid risk platforms; enterprise-only.
idea: A lightweight tracker that links supplier locations to public events and scores disruption risk with transparent rules and an evaluation on past incidents.
novelty: Hypothesis: transparent low-cost version is useful for small firms. Commercial tools exist; differentiation is cost and explainability.
stack: Python, RSS/news APIs, GDELT or similar open events, geocoding, SQLite, simple dashboard
stages: Define supplier list -> ingest events -> match by location/industry -> rule scoring -> backtest on 5 known disruptions
risks: Noisy news, geocoding errors, false alarms.
metrics: Lead time before known disruptions, precision of alerts
prior_art: supply chain risk monitoring open data

name: FewShotQC: few-shot visual defect detection for small electronics workshops
problem: Small shops lack labelled defect data, so standard supervised inspection models do not apply.
verify: Review MVTec AD and PCB defect datasets; ask a workshop what defects cost them.
existing: Commercial AOI machines, PatchCore/anomaly-detection papers.
idea: Train on good boards only (unsupervised anomaly detection such as PatchCore) and measure how few reference images are needed on real PCB photos.
novelty: Hypothesis: performance versus number of good samples on a small real dataset. Method is existing; evaluation is the contribution.
stack: PyTorch, anomalib, OpenCV, Raspberry Pi/phone camera, lighting rig
stages: Reproduce on MVTec -> capture own PCB images -> train on N good samples -> test injected defects -> latency on Pi
risks: Lighting variance, few real defects to test.
metrics: AUROC vs number of training images, false rejects per 100 boards

name: SlopeSense: low-cost tilt and rainfall nodes for landslide early warning
problem: Hill communities face landslides with little warning; professional instrumentation is costly.
verify: Read GSI/NDMA landslide data and low-cost sensor pilot studies; check rainfall-threshold literature.
existing: Professional inclinometers, rainfall-threshold systems, a few IIT/Amrita pilot networks.
idea: Solar LoRa nodes with MEMS tilt and soil-moisture sensors plus rainfall thresholds; validate on a lab slope model before any field use.
novelty: Hypothesis: cheap tilt plus moisture trend improves early warning over rainfall alone. Pilots exist, so cite and compare.
stack: ESP32/nRF, MEMS inclinometer, soil moisture probe, LoRa, solar, Python analysis
stages: Sensor characterisation -> lab slope tank with induced failure -> thresholds -> LoRa link tests -> field-readiness review with experts
risks: Safety and false alarms; do not deploy as a warning system without expert validation.
metrics: Detection lead time in lab failures, false alarm rate, power autonomy

name: FloodBench: honest comparison of simple and ML river-flood forecasts on open hydrology data
problem: ML flood forecasts are reported with weak baselines and leakage-prone splits.
verify: Read Kratzert et al. LSTM hydrology work and the Caravan dataset documentation.
existing: Google Flood Hub, GloFAS, NeuralHydrology.
idea: Benchmark persistence and linear baselines against an LSTM using strict time-based splits on open catchments, including lead-time degradation.
novelty: Hypothesis: skill gain over strong baselines is smaller than headlines suggest at longer leads.
stack: Python, Caravan dataset, NeuralHydrology, scikit-learn
stages: Pick 30 catchments -> baselines -> LSTM -> time-split evaluation -> lead-time curves -> write-up
risks: Compute; regional generalisation; do not present as an operational warning.
metrics: NSE/KGE vs lead time, skill over persistence

name: FieldChange: Sentinel-2 change detection for flood extent and crop stress
problem: Farmers and responders lack timely, cheap maps of flood damage and crop stress.
verify: Review Copernicus Sentinel-2/-1 availability and existing flood-mapping products.
existing: Copernicus EMS, Google Earth Engine tutorials, ISRO Bhuvan.
idea: A reproducible pipeline using open Sentinel data to map water extent and NDVI change, validated against reference maps for past events.
novelty: Hypothesis: a simple, documented pipeline with uncertainty maps for one region. Many products exist; evaluation is local.
stack: Python, rasterio, Earth Engine or Copernicus API, scikit-learn
stages: Pick 2 past events -> download scenes -> water index + thresholds -> compare with reference -> NDVI change -> uncertainty
risks: Cloud cover, resolution limits.
metrics: IoU vs reference flood maps, processing time

name: CellHealth: battery state-of-health estimation compared across public datasets
problem: Battery packs degrade unpredictably; estimators trained on one chemistry often fail on another.
verify: Read NASA Ames, CALCE and Oxford battery dataset papers.
existing: BMS vendor algorithms, many dataset-specific papers.
idea: Compare simple capacity-trend models and ML across datasets to quantify transfer failure and propose a minimal feature set.
novelty: Hypothesis: cross-dataset evaluation exposes overfitting hidden by single-dataset results.
stack: Python, pandas, scikit-learn, PyTorch, public battery datasets
stages: Load 3 datasets -> baseline -> models -> cross-dataset tests -> feature ablation
risks: Datasets differ in protocol; limited real-world conditions.
metrics: RMSE of SoH across datasets, degradation of cross-dataset error

name: AirCal: calibrate low-cost PM2.5 sensors against reference stations
problem: Cheap PM sensors are biased by humidity; uncorrected readings mislead communities.
verify: Read EPA/AQ-SPEC low-cost sensor evaluations and CPCB station data availability.
existing: PurpleAir correction formulas, CPCB reference stations.
idea: Co-locate a sensor near a reference station, learn a humidity correction, and report error with intervals.
novelty: Hypothesis: local correction quality for Indian conditions. Mostly applied engineering.
stack: ESP32, PMS5003/SPS30, SHT4x, Python regression, CPCB open data
stages: Log data -> co-locate -> fit corrections -> validate on later weeks -> publish calibration notes
risks: Sensor drift; reference data gaps.
metrics: RMSE/MAE vs reference before and after, drift per month

name: AlarmSense: false-alarm reduction on open ICU waveform alarm data
problem: Most bedside alarms are false, causing alarm fatigue and missed real events.
verify: Read the PhysioNet/CinC 2015 false-alarm challenge paper.
existing: Challenge entries, vendor algorithms.
idea: Reproduce top challenge methods, evaluate generalisation across alarm types and signal quality, and report sensitivity-first metrics.
novelty: Hypothesis: signal-quality gating improves specificity without losing sensitivity. No clinical claims.
stack: Python, wfdb, scikit-learn, PhysioNet open data
stages: Reproduce baseline -> signal quality index -> cross-alarm evaluation -> sensitivity constraints -> report
risks: Must not suppress true alarms; research-only.
metrics: Sensitivity and specificity per alarm type, missed true alarms

name: NeuroCheck: cross-session reliability of motor-imagery EEG classifiers on open datasets
problem: BCI accuracy claims fall sharply across sessions and subjects, limiting real use.
verify: Read MOABB benchmark papers and BCI reproducibility reviews.
existing: MOABB, OpenBCI community projects, deep-learning EEG papers.
idea: Reproduce several classifiers and quantify cross-session and cross-subject drops, then test simple recalibration.
novelty: Hypothesis: lightweight recalibration recovers a large share of lost accuracy. Evaluation-driven.
stack: Python, MNE, MOABB, PyTorch, open datasets (BNCI)
stages: Run MOABB baselines -> cross-session tests -> recalibration variants -> statistics -> report
risks: EEG variability; small effect sizes.
metrics: Accuracy drop across sessions, recovery after recalibration with N trials

name: LearnLoop: offline spaced-repetition tutor evaluated on a small student cohort
problem: Students in low-connectivity settings lack adaptive practice tools that work offline.
verify: Read spaced-repetition efficacy studies; talk to teachers about connectivity.
existing: Anki, Khan Academy offline, Duolingo.
idea: A PWA with an FSRS-style scheduler for a single subject and a small A/B study against fixed-order review.
novelty: Hypothesis: measured retention gain in a real class. Tools exist; the contribution is the study.
stack: PWA, IndexedDB, FSRS algorithm, small analytics export
stages: Pick topic -> build scheduler -> content -> two-group pilot -> retention test after 2 weeks
risks: Small sample sizes; consent and child-privacy rules.
metrics: Retention score difference, completion rate

name: FlakeHunter: detect and rank flaky tests from CI history
problem: Flaky tests waste developer time and hide real failures.
verify: Read flaky-test studies (Google, Luo et al.) and sample GitHub Actions histories.
existing: Google internal tooling, pytest-rerunfailures, commercial CI analytics.
idea: Mine CI run history, flag tests whose outcome changes without code change, and rank by cost.
novelty: Hypothesis: a simple statistical detector captures most flakiness. Mostly engineering.
stack: Python, GitHub API, pandas, a small dashboard
stages: Collect histories from 20 public repos -> detector -> validate by re-running -> ranking report
risks: API limits; confirming ground truth costs CI time.
metrics: Precision of flagged tests on re-run, developer hours saved (estimated)

name: SmokeWatch: early wildfire-smoke detection from low-cost cameras on a Raspberry Pi
problem: Wildfires are found late; satellite revisit times leave gaps and ground cameras are expensive.
verify: Read FIgLib/HPWREN smoke-camera work and Indian forest-fire statistics (FSI).
existing: HPWREN/ALERTWildfire cameras, commercial AI fire detection.
idea: Edge detector trained on public smoke images with temporal filtering to cut false alarms from clouds and dust.
novelty: Hypothesis: temporal consistency halves false alarms. Existing systems are stronger; evaluate honestly.
stack: Raspberry Pi 5, camera, YOLO-nano or MobileNet, OpenCV, FIgLib dataset
stages: Reproduce baseline -> temporal filter -> collect cloud/dust negatives -> Pi latency -> alert logic
risks: False alarms; do not rely on it as safety system; deployment permissions.
metrics: Detection delay, false alarms per camera-day

name: SoilMesh: calibrated low-cost soil-moisture sensing for irrigation decisions
problem: Over- and under-watering waste water and yield; cheap capacitive sensors are inconsistent across soils.
verify: Find ICAR/FAO irrigation efficiency figures and capacitive-sensor calibration papers.
existing: Commercial probes, ESP32 hobby projects with uncalibrated sensors.
idea: Calibrate capacitive sensors per soil type against gravimetric moisture and drive a simple irrigation rule, measuring water saved in a pot trial.
novelty: Hypothesis: per-soil calibration makes cheap sensors usable. Engineering with a measured trial.
stack: ESP32, capacitive sensors, LoRa/BLE, Python calibration
stages: Gravimetric calibration -> sensor drift test -> irrigation rule -> two-group pot trial -> water-use comparison
risks: Biology timescales; soil variability.
metrics: Calibration error (vol. % moisture), water used vs control, plant outcome

name: RetinaShift: honest diabetic-retinopathy screening on low-cost phone fundus images
problem: Diabetic retinopathy causes preventable blindness, and screening programmes lack retina specialists; models trained on hospital-grade fundus cameras often degrade on cheap smartphone adapters.
verify: Read national diabetes/DR prevalence reports and screening-programme coverage; ask two ophthalmologists how phone-captured images are used today.
existing: Regulator-cleared autonomous DR screening systems on desktop fundus cameras; academic models on EyePACS/APTOS/IDRiD; a few phone-adapter studies.
idea: Quantify and reduce the accuracy drop from clinic cameras to phone adapters with image-quality gating, test-time adaptation and a 'refer when unsure' policy.
novelty: Hypothesis: a calibrated quality-gate + abstention policy keeps referral sensitivity on phone images close to clinic images. Must check recent phone-fundus DR literature first.
stack: Python, PyTorch, timm, public fundus datasets (APTOS, IDRiD, Messidor-2), Android/TFLite for the demo
stages: Baseline on clinic datasets -> simulate phone degradations (blur, glare, vignetting) -> quality gate -> test-time adaptation -> calibration + abstention -> per-device error analysis
hw: Laptop/GPU (Colab works); optional clip-on phone fundus lens
risks: Medical-device regulation; simulated degradation may not match real phones; never present as diagnostic.
metrics: Referable-DR sensitivity/specificity, AUROC per capture device, abstention rate, expected calibration error
prior_art: smartphone fundus diabetic retinopathy deep learning
test-time adaptation medical imaging domain shift

name: AMRWatch: early warning of rising antibiotic resistance from routine lab antibiograms
problem: Hospitals produce susceptibility results daily but resistance trends are usually reviewed yearly, so local surges are noticed late.
verify: Read WHO GLASS and national AMR surveillance reports; ask a hospital microbiologist how often antibiograms are updated and who acts on them.
existing: WHONET for lab data management, national surveillance networks, published annual antibiograms; research on resistance forecasting.
idea: Statistical change-point and seasonal-baseline detection on organism-antibiotic resistance rates, with small-sample-aware alerts and a weekly ward-level report.
novelty: Hypothesis: Bayesian small-count alerts give earlier, fewer-false-alarm warnings than yearly antibiograms. Probably an improved implementation rather than a new mechanism.
stack: Python, pandas, PyMC or statsmodels, Streamlit, WHONET-format synthetic or public AMR data
stages: Data model -> synthetic data with injected surges -> baselines (yearly %, CUSUM) -> Bayesian alerting -> report -> evaluation on held-out years
risks: Real lab data needs ethics approval; testing-bias (only sick patients are cultured) distorts rates.
metrics: Detection delay for injected surges, false alerts per month, precision of alerts reviewed by a microbiologist
prior_art: antimicrobial resistance trend detection change point

name: OTFlow: operating-theatre scheduling that learns real surgery durations
problem: Booked surgery times are often wrong, causing overruns, cancellations and idle theatres in busy hospitals.
verify: Find published theatre-utilisation and same-day cancellation rates; interview a theatre coordinator about how slots are booked.
existing: Hospital information systems with booking modules; operations-research papers on surgical scheduling; commercial perioperative analytics.
idea: Predict case duration with quantile regression from procedure/surgeon/patient features, then schedule with a stochastic optimiser that limits overrun probability.
novelty: Hypothesis: quantile predictions + chance-constrained scheduling cut overruns versus mean-duration booking. Well-studied area; value is an honest open benchmark.
stack: Python, LightGBM quantile regression, OR-Tools CP-SAT, synthetic data from published duration distributions
stages: Synthetic data -> duration model -> baseline scheduler -> chance-constrained scheduler -> simulation over months -> sensitivity analysis
risks: No real data without a hospital partner; human factors dominate real scheduling.
metrics: Overrun minutes/day, cancellations, utilisation, pinball loss of duration predictions
prior_art: surgical case duration prediction machine learning
stochastic operating room scheduling chance constraint

name: FairFlow: cash-flow credit scoring for thin-file borrowers with a built-in fairness audit
problem: Many small borrowers have no credit history, so bureau scores exclude them; cash-flow data could help but can encode bias.
verify: Read RBI/World Bank financial-inclusion data and Account Aggregator adoption reports; check published studies on cash-flow underwriting performance.
existing: Lender cash-flow underwriting models, Account Aggregator framework, fairness toolkits (Fairlearn, AIF360), academic credit-scoring benchmarks.
idea: Engineer features from synthetic bank-statement transactions, compare against a bureau-only baseline, and ship an automatic fairness and explanation report per model version.
novelty: Hypothesis: a small set of interpretable cash-flow features gives most of the lift with auditable fairness. Synthetic data only.
stack: Python, pandas, LightGBM, SHAP, Fairlearn, synthetic transaction generator
stages: Transaction simulator -> feature library -> baseline vs cash-flow model -> fairness metrics across groups -> reason codes -> model card
risks: Synthetic data may not reflect reality; lending regulation; never use real personal data without consent.
metrics: AUC/KS vs baseline, approval rate at fixed default rate, demographic parity and equal-opportunity gaps
